text: Specifies: if you need to transmit the data packet, then you have to sense the channel for peaks. If instead you are the access point and you need to transmit the beacon, you need to sense the channel as idle for peaks, right? So that's a very detailed specification of how to apply the general principle. So saying that CSMA, for example, CA is DCF plus because is not accurate, okay? Because CSMA and also CA collision avoidance is a general approach. DCF is the specific channel access scheme that details how the nodes behave in the different situations. It applies the general principle, but it's a specific channel access scheme. And indeed, we have in sensors that, for example, here we said we are applying also here carrier sensing multiple access collision avoidance, right? But is this the same as DCF? No, it's a difference. Okay, see the difference. The other thing: DCF is indeed a channel access scheme that includes the because mechanism. So saying DCF plus because does not make sense. Okay, the because is a mechanism that is part of DCF. The because is there as a mechanism as a procedure in order to avoid collisions.
